evals.name: small-python-repo-from-readme
evals.prompt: Make this repo agent-ready so AI coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Copilot) work in it efficiently and cheaply. The current directory is a flattened snapshot of the orders-service repo: README.md is the only documentation, the runnable commands are spread across the Makefile, package.json scripts and deploy.sh, and .github-ci.yml is our current .github/workflows/ci.yml (flattened here; write the new one at .github/workflows/ci.yml). Set up whatever agent entrypoint files, docs layout, task runner, tool pinning, git hooks, CI wiring and guardrail checks you think an agent-optimised repo needs, keeping every command and every rule from the README available. Do not run or install anything and do not ask questions - just write the files in the current directory. Finish with a short NOTES.md stating, with numbers, what an agent had to load before starting work in this repo before your change and after it.
evals.expected_output: CLAUDE.md is exactly @AGENTS.md; an AGENTS.md within 150 lines / 2000 tokens that tells agents to reuse the Taskfile and carries every README rule inline (Decimal, structlog, flags.yaml, the domain import rule); for a repo this small (README under 1000 tokens) no docs/ and no docs/README.md hop; Taskfile.yml absorbing every Makefile/package.json/deploy.sh command with desc lines and a ci task; mise.toml; hooks and a thin CI workflow that run task ci; a bootstrap for environments without task; README rules preserved; cold-start numbers reported

downstream.prompt: Write ANSWER.md containing (1) the exact command to run only the unit test test_discount in tests/unit/test_pricing.py and (2) the command or commands that must pass before pushing. Do not run anything; write the file only.

Add a way to run the integration tests with coverage (pytest tests/integration -q --cov=orders) that follows how this repo already defines its runnable commands, and write ANSWER.md saying how a contributor invokes it. Do not run anything; write files only.

Add the convention 'Refund amounts are stored in minor units as Decimal, never float' where this repo keeps its conventions, so that both contributors and AI agents will find it. Do not run anything; write files only.

The last production deploy is broken and must be rolled back, and a teammate's alembic run says the target database is not up to date. Write ANSWER.md with exactly what to run for each, in order, and every constraint this repo puts on a production deploy. Do not run anything; write the file only.

evals.name: fat-claude-md-restructure
evals.prompt: Our CLAUDE.md has grown into a wall of text that Claude keeps ignoring parts of, and it only helps Claude - Codex and Copilot users get nothing. Restructure this repo (the notify service; the current directory holds its CLAUDE.md, RUNBOOK.md and package.json) so every agent gets a small, shared entrypoint and loads detail only when a task needs it, and so the pnpm scripts have a single discoverable home with git hooks and CI running the same checks. Nothing currently in CLAUDE.md or RUNBOOK.md may be lost - relocate it. Do not run or install anything and do not ask questions - just write the files in the current directory. Finish with a short NOTES.md stating, with numbers, what an agent loaded at start before your change and what it loads now.
evals.expected_output: CLAUDE.md becomes exactly @AGENTS.md; AGENTS.md within 150 lines / 2000 tokens carrying the commands, layout and every rule most tasks need (PII logging, generated files, migrate reset, factories) inline; long-form content (channel and API references, runbook, deployment) relocated into docs/ behind explicit "before you X, read docs/Y" routes, with docs/README.md as the catch-all at most two hops deep; nothing lost; Taskfile.yml wrapping every pnpm script with desc lines and a ci task; mise.toml pinning node/pnpm/task; hooks and a thin workflow running task ci; a bootstrap for environments without task; before/after cold-start numbers reported
